newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil power privatization seen at $4 bln in '97.
newsitem.headline: Brazil power privatization seen at $4 bln in '97.

text.p: Brazilian Mines and Energy Minister Raimundo Brito said the government stood to earn between $3 billion and $4 billion this year from privatizations and concessions in the power sector.

He said private investment in the electricity sector since the start of President Fernando Henrique Cardoso's administration already amounted to $14 billion, with $4.6 billion to $4.7 billion deriving from privatizations.

The list of power companies to be sold this year include state power utilities Coelba (Bahia), Energipe (Sergipe), Enersul (Mato Grosso do Sul), CEEE (Rio Grande do Sul), CPFL (Sao Paulo), Cachoeira Dourada hydroelectric plant, and Sao Paulo state generator CESP.

Brito told reporters he expected all federally-owned power generators to be privatized by the end of 1998, with the exception of the Itaipu hydroelectric plant and nuclear power plants which are not up for privatization.

Brazil's National Development Bank has already contracted two advisors for the privatization of federal power generators Furnas and Eletrosul and is still in the process of finding advisors for the sale of Eletronorte and Chesf. ((-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
